import os
from google.cloud import vision

def score_image_safety(image_path):
    """
    Checks an image for unsafe or policy-sensitive visual content using Google Cloud Vision AI.
    """
    # Instantiates a client
    client = vision.ImageAnnotatorClient()

    # Loads the image into memory
    with open(image_path, 'rb') as image_file:
        content = image_file.read()

    image = vision.Image(content=content)

    # Performs label detection on the image
    response = client.safe_search_detection(image=image)
    safe_search_annotation = response.safe_search_annotation

    print(f"Safe search results for {image_path}:")
    print(f"Adult: {vision.Likelihood(safe_search_annotation.adult).name}")
    print(f"Medical: {vision.Likelihood(safe_search_annotation.medical).name}")
    print(f"Spoof: {vision.Likelihood(safe_search_annotation.spoof).name}")
    print(f"Violence: {vision.Likelihood(safe_search_annotation.violence).name}")
    print(f"Racy: {vision.Likelihood(safe_search_annotation.racy).name}")

    return safe_search_annotation

if __name__ == '__main__':
    # For demonstration purposes, you would replace 'your_image.jpg' with an actual image path
    # and ensure GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS environment variable is set.
    # For example:
    # export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="/path/to/your/keyfile.json"
    # python score_image_safety.py your_image.jpg
    
    # You can provide an image path as a command-line argument or modify this directly
    if len(os.sys.argv) > 1:
        image_file_path = os.sys.argv[1]
    else:
        print("Please provide an image path as an argument. Example: python score_image_safety.py your_image.jpg")
        os.sys.exit(1)

    score_image_safety(image_file_path)

import os
from google.cloud import vision

def detect_text(image_path):
    """Detects text in the image file."""
    client = vision.ImageAnnotatorClient()

    with open(image_path, "rb") as image_file:
        content = image_file.read()

    image = vision.Image(content=content)

    response = client.text_detection(image=image)
    texts = response.text_annotations
    print("Texts:")

    for text in texts:
        print(f'\n"{text.description}"')

    if response.error.message:
        raise Exception(
            "{}
For more info on error messages, check: "
            "https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors".format(response.error.message)
        )

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Replace 'path/to/your/image.jpg' with the actual path to your image file
    # Ensure GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS environment variable is set or
    # authenticate using other methods as described in Google Cloud Vision API documentation.
    # Example: export GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS="/path/to/your/keyfile.json"
    
    # You can provide the image path as a command-line argument,
    # or modify this line to point to your image.
    image_file_path = "path/to/your/image.jpg" 
    # For demonstration, you might want to create a dummy image or provide a real path.
    # Example: image_file_path = "image.jpg" 

    if os.path.exists(image_file_path):
        detect_text(image_file_path)
    else:
        print(f"Error: Image file not found at '{image_file_path}'. Please update the image_file_path variable.")

from google.cloud import vision
import os

def describe_image(image_path):
    """Generates a short visual description for an image using Google Cloud Vision API."""

    # Set up Google Cloud credentials
    # os.environ["GOOGLE_APPLICATION_CREDENTIALS"] = "path/to/your/keyfile.json"

    client = vision.ImageAnnotatorClient()

    with open(image_path, 'rb') as image_file:
        content = image_file.read()

    image = vision.Image(content=content)

    response = client.label_detection(image=image)
    labels = response.label_annotations

    if labels:
        description = "This image likely contains: " + ", ".join([label.description for label in labels])
        print(description)
    else:
        print("No visual description could be generated for the image.")

if __name__ == "__main__":
    # Replace with the actual path to your image
    image_to_describe = "path/to/your/image.jpg"
    describe_image(image_to_describe)

import io
import os

from google.cloud import vision_v1p1beta1 as vision

def detect_labels(image_path):
    """Detects labels in the image file."""
    client = vision.ImageAnnotatorClient()

    with io.open(image_path, 'rb') as image_file:
        content = image_file.read()

    image = vision.Image(content=content)

    response = client.label_detection(image=image)
    labels = response.label_annotations
    print('Labels:')

    for label in labels:
        print(label.description)

if __name__ == '__main__':
    # Replace 'path/to/your/image.jpg' with the actual path to your image file
